startup/no match.reason: what 0.1.0 adds at start, counted without the dynamic loader's own instructions (startup/loader has those). On the AWS build box 2, release builds with symbols kept, callgrind: 424,755 -> 440,115 outside the loader from e7d6c9d9 to 24da6b5e (1.036), and the gate itself on CI's own binaries of e7d6c9d9 and 24da6b5e 428,844 -> 441,957 to 441,985 over two runs (1.0306). The ratio moves with build settings: a release build with symbols kept reads 1.036 and a release build on box 2 1.0409, so the limit is judged on the runner. There it read 1.0351 at 0ff04aa6, 1.0394 at 5abc1066 and 1.0342 at 3e170b46 (Rust 1.100.0, edition 2024): headroom about 1.6%. What moved 0ff04aa6 to 5abc1066 (+2,023 on the runner) is no code of scrutate's: on one box the two CI binaries differ by +1,938 under cachegrind, of which scrutate's own code is +12 and the rest glibc's sscanf and strtoul as pthread_getattr_np reads /proc/self/maps for the main thread's stack guard at std's start, the same 51 lines each time, costing more with the addresses and sizes a binary's layout gives its mappings; it is layout, and nothing in the code avoids it. So a reading of this row can move by about 2,000 instructions (0.4%) between two builds whose code on grep's path is the same: a change under that size is layout until a count by function says otherwise. In main, 423,511 -> 436,694: the one new cost is the walker's index-file guard (files.rs climb, 14,328 instructions, 17bc4b4b and c46ff23c, with 8 more statx and 1 more getcwd), about 6.2 K of it hashing each ancestor's PathBuf component by component into a SipHash set; hashing the canonical path's bytes with InoHasher and one buffer per climb is the candidate for after 0.1.0. Absolute counts differ between the runner and a box by about 170 K, so only ratios on one machine mean anything; the same binary twice reads within 0.12%. The limit leaves room for the layout band R3X-17a measured (0.64%)

startup/loader.reason: the dynamic loader's own instructions in the start-up row, reported so that growth there is seen, not because a user waits on it: they follow the binary's count of relative relocations, about 16 instructions each (35,488 at e7d6c9d9, 36,398 at 24da6b5e on box 2; 769,804 -> 784,567, 1.019, and 768,688 -> 783,273 on CI's own binaries), which every static table adds to. A planted table of 20,000 pointers adds 240,000 here and nothing to startup/no match; a planted constructor adds to startup/no match and nothing here. Absolute counts differ between the runner and a box by about 170 K, so only ratios on one machine mean anything

binheavy/literal.reason: the NUL rules: a walked file with a NUL byte answered as ripgrep reads it (FUZZ-02, R3X-14c), with two more of ripgrep's answers copied, a walked file whose NUL comes after its first 64 KiB (R4-FZ-01) and the context separator before the binary note under --sort (R4-FZ-02). CI's benchmarks run at e2d39d85 (run 43782004117): 85,902,359 -> 87,809,435, 1.0222, about 100 instructions per binary file over R3X-14c; R3X-14d and R3X-14e took most of it back (the Collector built in place and the calls around it inlined, about 40 per walked file). bench/instructions.py on an AWS build box after R3X-14e: 80,264,698 -> 81,295,843, 1.0128 against main e7d6c9d9. ripgrep 15.2.0 counts 1.24 times main on the smaller tree the rows were also checked on
